messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The bug occurs because StringUtils.containsAny(CharSequence, char[]) method operates on individual char units and does not correctly handle Unicode supplementary characters, which are represented as surrogate pairs (two char values). In the containsAny method, the input CharSequence is iterated character-by-character using charAt(i), which only returns one 16-bit code unit. Supplemental characters require two code units together to form a single logical character.

The method compares each char from the input sequence to chars in the search array. Because supplementary characters are split into two chars, the method wrongly treats each half of the surrogate pair as an independent character rather than a combined single code point. This leads to incorrect matching: the method might falsely match or fail to differentiate between supplementary characters like U+20000 and U+20001, which differ by their low surrogate char.

The other containsAny overload that takes a String delegates to this char[] method after converting the string into a char array, so it has the same limitation.

The failing test calls containsAny with CharU20000 and CharU20001, i.e. supplementary characters stored as surrogate pairs. Because the method only compares chars, it may return an incorrect match result.

Hence, the root cause is that containsAny methods do not handle supplementary characters by recognizing surrogate pairs and comparing whole code points. Instead, they operate on UTF-16 code units only, which produces incorrect results for Unicode 2.0+ supplementary characters.

Next, I could examine any related methods that might handle supplementary characters properly (like those using codePointAt or similar) or verify if there are tests or comments about this limitation.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The fault occurs because the StringUtils.containsAny method that takes a CharSequence and a char array iterates over the character sequence one UTF-16 code unit (char) at a time. It compares these individual chars with the chars in the search array. Since Unicode supplementary characters (those beyond U+FFFF, such as U+20000) are represented in UTF-16 using surrogate pairs (two chars), the method effectively treats each half of a surrogate pair as an independent character. This leads to incorrect behavior when searching for supplementary characters because the method never compares full Unicode code points but only single 16-bit code units. Consequently, it can falsely report matches or misses when supplementary characters are involved. The containsAny method overload that takes a String delegates to this char array version after converting the string to a char array, thus also shares this limitation. The failing test case checks for containment of two supplementary characters represented as surrogate pairs and expects a false result, but the current implementation does not handle surrogate pairs properly and thus fails this check. This diagnosis explains the symptom reported in the bug report and the failing test.
